title: Word: Copilot Agent Mode edits documents through chat
summary: Hold: the claim that Microsoft has not published licensing specific to Agent Mode is too broad. Microsoft's support documentation explicitly identifies the former Agent Mode experience as editing with Copilot and names eligible plans; the roadmap facts and licence-assignment controls are supported.

claims.quote: Searched: Agent Mode Word enabled by default; Word Agent Mode default admin. Read record, Current Channel Agent mode entry, Copilot release notes and editing-with-Copilot support. Default-editing text names 557673, not 499428.

claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to Agent Mode is not yet published.
claims.quote: Editing with Copilot in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word is a way to create content within the Microsoft Copilot experience for Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, and Premium plans. ... In previous releases, this was marketed as "Agent Mode"
claims.fix: Remove 'A licence requirement' from the absence sentence. Replace the sentence with 'A meter or credit rate specific to Agent Mode is not yet published.' Keep the preceding, supported enterprise service-description licence requirement; do not import the consumer plans into enterprise prerequisites.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences in the admin centre requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Graph licence assignment requires User.ReadWrite.All or another permission listed in the Assign license Graph reference.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the 'Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page.
